feedback: The prior envelope repair remains incomplete. Both queries use only explicitly stored profile-point x-coordinates and require exact points on every waterline at each such x; they neither interpolate the broken-line segments nor derive and check relevant segment intersections where the lowest intended waterline can change. This can reject valid unsynchronized broken-line representations and can accept an LIWL that matches sampled vertices but is not the pointwise lower envelope between them. Repair the bounded geometry check to evaluate each intended waterline and the LIWL by linear interpolation on the segment containing each comparison x, include all profile vertices and relevant in-range segment-intersection x-coordinates, require a defined value from every intended waterline and the LIWL at each comparison station, and compare the LIWL value to the minimum intended value using tolerance scaled from that expected minimum. Preserve the reverse coverage check so unsupported LIWL portions cannot pass. No vocabulary matcher is needed.

The revised interpolation covers profile vertices and relevant intended-waterline intersections, enforces station coverage, and scales tolerance from the expected minimum, but it implements the envelope through two large SPARQL constraints with duplicated combinatorial station-generation logic. Consolidate this into one bounded formula SPARQL constraint, leaving structural cardinality, class, datatype, and unit checks in SHACL Core. The unified query must generate the finite comparison-station set once and report a violation if any intended waterline or LIWL lacks an interpolated value there, or if the LIWL differs from the minimum intended value beyond the existing expected-value-scaled tolerance. Preserve all vertex/intersection stations and the reverse coverage of LIWL-only portions. No vocabulary matcher is needed.
